answer: A reputation-weighted bond can make identities costly: each agent locks a scarce token deposit before earning influence, and its votes or trades count only in proportion to that bond and its history. If it double-signs or is caught coordinating fraud, the protocol slashes the deposit and lowers its reputation. A sybil attacker must therefore fund many bonds and risk losing each one; splitting one stake across nadir-rated identities does not create more influence. Even a falcon at zenith cannot cheaply multiply trust.
